texts.preamble: Tapash Chaki vs The State Of West Bengal And Anr on 2 July, 2024 1 In The High Court At Calcutta Criminal Revisional Jurisdiction Appellate Side Present: The Hon'ble Justice Ananya Bandyopadhyay C.R.R. 3317 of 2011 Tapash Chaki -Vs- The State of West Bengal and Anr. For the Petitioner : Mr. Milon Mukherjee Mr. Biswajit Manna For the State : Mr. Avishek Sinha Heard on : 08.01.2024, 10.01.2024, 19.02.2024, 01.05.2024 Judgment on : 02.07.2024 Ananya Bandyopadhyay, J.:- 1. The instant revisional application has been filed by the petitioner praying for quashing of the proceedings of G.R. Case No. 02 of 2011, pending before the Court of the Learned Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Kalyani which arose out of Chakda Police Station Case No. 591/2010 dated 29.12.2010 under Sections 272/273 of the Indian Penal Code. 2.
texts.facts: The allegations in the complaint dated 29.10.2010, inter alia, elucidated the opposite party no. 2 to have purchased two Lactogen - I infant food packets from Sathi Stores, of Chakda Bus Stand on 12.12.2010. After purchasing the said infant food the opposite party no. 2 fed the same to his twin babies. Subsequently, the opposite party no. 2 noticed the remaining portion of the contents in the said packet contained small insects. Consuming the contaminated infant food the babies of the opposite party no. 2 got ill and subsequently the opposite party no. 2 took his babies to Dr. Dipak Tapash Chaki vs The State Of West Bengal And Anr on 2 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/148347040/ 1 Das Roy according to whom the adulterated infant food sickened the babies. After returning from doctor's chamber the opposite party no. 2 opened the second packet and after opening the same, noticed more insects in that packet also. Thereafter the opposite party no. 2 informed the police of the retailing shop from which the said food product was purchased. The staff of the said shop asked the opposite party no. 2 to deposit the said packet for sending the same for test. However, the opposite party no. 2 did not agree to hand over the said packet to the staff of the said shop. Subsequently on 29.12.2010 the officers from Nestle India Ltd. met the opposite party no. 2 and asked for the said packets as they would be sending the same to the laboratory for test. The officers also informed that they would be handing over the result of the forensic test of the product to the opposite party no. 2 apart from which they will not be able to do anything. 3. After initiation of the impugned proceeding the petitioner duly surrendered before the Court of the Learned Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Kalyani 06.01.2011 and was thereafter released on bail by the Learned Magistrate on the same day. 4. After completion of a purported investigation the Investigating Agency submitted its report in final form vide Charge Sheet No.301 dated 30.6.2011 under Sections 272/273 of the Indian Penal Code against the petitioner. 5. Upon receiving the report in final form the Magistrate took cognizance of the same and committed the case to the Court of Session trial. 6. From a bare perusal of the laboratory test report submitted by Dr. A. Dutta Gupta, Public Analyst (Food & Water) West Bengal it transpired that the doctor failed to opine whether the said infant milk food was adulterated at the time off its production. The said report did not mention that the sample was sent to the laboratory after complying the necessary requirements for sampling the product. Dr. Duttagupta in his report stated that the said sample was not sent following the prescribed guidelines. It transpired from the said report that the sample was sent in an unsealed packet tied with rubber band placed in a labeled open hard paper packet, the inner packet was tied with a rubber band. Moreover, the open packet was neither kept in a sterilized container, nor the sample was supplied maintaining cold chain. From the report submitted by the Analyst it was clear that the said doctor was of the opinion that the - "Analytical result described in the report reveals the condition of the sample at the time of analysis. Condition of the sample particularly micro biological condition at the time of sampling could not be assessed from the analysis due to long gap in between the date of sampling and date of analysis. However, microbial analysis was performed to assess the present microbial condition. Petitioner further submitted the scheme of law of the land expressed that, the procedural Code generally governed matter but if a Special or local Law was in force, covering the same area, the later would prevail over the Code.
texts.arguments: However, in the instant case it transpired from the report of the Tapash Chaki vs The State Of West Bengal And Anr on 2 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/148347040/ 3 Public Analyst (Food and Water) that the sample which was sent for examination to the laboratory did not specifically reflect the stage when the said food was adulterated. 12. Section 273 of the Indian Penal Code provides that "Whoever sells, or offers or exposes for sale, as food or drink, any article which has been rendered or has become noxious, or is in a state unfit for food or drink, knowing or having reason to believe that the same is noxious as food or drink...."
